interest: This file offers valuable historical insight into the complex jurisdictional interplay between state banking authorities and federal wartime agencies in liquidating enemy assets during World War II. It illustrates how the closure of a major financial institution like the Yokohama Specie Bank rippled through international commercial networks across Latin America, giving rise to diplomatic inquiries from the Dominican Republic regarding outstanding commercial paper and intricate cross-border transaction tracing in Argentina and Brazil. Additionally, the collection documents the procedural mechanisms established for American holders of Japanese dollar bonds following the outbreak of hostilities and captures early 1941 inter-agency intelligence coordination on Japanese banking between the State Department, the FBI, and the Treasury Department.
keywords: Superintendent of Banks of the State of New York
Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.51611, covering January 1941 through December 1944) documents the extraterritorial, domestic legal, financial, and diplomatic ramifications of the closure and liquidation of Japanese banking branches in the United States—primarily the New York agency of the Yokohama Specie Bank, Ltd.—following the outbreak of the Pacific War. Key issues addressed include the division of authority between state regulators (the Superintendent of Banks of the State of New York) and federal wartime agencies (the Alien Property Custodian and the Treasury Department's Foreign Funds Control), diplomatic inquiries from the Dominican Republic regarding the collection of pre-war commercial drafts drawn by Osaka firm Sanko & Co., cross-border financial tracing involving the Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires and Banco do Brasil in Argentina, instructions to bondholders regarding claims on Japanese dollar bonds, and pre-war intelligence coordination between the FBI, State Department, and Treasury concerning Japanese banking operations.

subfiles.about: Notice informing holders of Japanese dollar bonds that the New York branch of the Yokohama Specie Bank is being liquidated and enclosing claim forms.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Bondholders Protective Council advises holders of dollar bonds issued by the Japanese Government, the cities of Tokyo and Yokohama, and the Taiwan Electric Power Company regarding the liquidation of the Yokohama Specie Bank's New York branch. Following the outbreak of the war, the New York State Superintendent of Banks took over the agency, which served as paying agent for these securities, and initiated liquidation proceedings. The notice transmits proof of claim forms and creditor notices for bondholders desiring to file claims against the bank's assets while clarifying that the Council cannot offer legal counsel.
subfiles.title: Circular Notice on Proof of Claim for Holders of Japanese Bonds
subfiles.to: Holders of Japanese Government, Municipal, and Corporate Bonds

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting a Dominican diplomatic note requesting clarification of the legal standing and authority of the New York Superintendent of Banks.
keywords: Superintendent of Banks of the State of New York
subfiles.summary: American Minister Avra M. Warren transmits a copy and translation of Dominican Foreign Office note no. 14057 to Secretary of State Cordell Hull. The Dominican Government sought clarification regarding whether the Superintendent of Banks of the State of New York functions as an official authority of the United States Government with legal capacity to collect outstanding Japanese commercial credits. Warren requests Department guidance to formulate an appropriate diplomatic reply to the Dominican authorities.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 958 from Ciudad Trujillo on Status of New York Superintendent of Banks

subfiles.about: Diplomatic note inquiring into the official status and legal authority of the New York Superintendent of Banks to demand commercial drafts of Sanko & Co.
subfiles.from: Dominican Republic Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs
keywords: The National City Bank of New York
subfiles.summary: The Dominican Foreign Ministry requests the U.S. Embassy to advise whether the New York Superintendent of Banks in charge of the Yokohama Specie Bank is an official of the U.S. Government entitled to collect commercial drafts drawn by Sanko & Co., Ltd. of Osaka against Dominican merchants. The note explains that a Japanese commercial representative had originally entrusted these drafts to the National City Bank of New York in Ciudad Trujillo for collection. The Dominican Government notes that the Superintendent has now demanded the return of these documents, prompting questions regarding his legal capacity.
subfiles.title: Note No. 14057 from Dominican Foreign Office on Sanko & Co. Commercial Drafts
subfiles.to: Embassy of the United States of America, Ciudad Trujillo

subfiles.about: English translation of Dominican Note No. 14057 regarding the legal authority of the New York Superintendent of Banks.
subfiles.from: Dominican Department of State for Foreign Affairs
keywords: National City Bank of New York
subfiles.summary: This official translation prepared by the U.S. Embassy in Ciudad Trujillo renders Dominican Note No. 14057 into English. It inquires whether the New York Superintendent of Banks possesses governmental authority and legal capacity to collect commercial paper issued by Sanko & Co., Ltd. of Osaka against Dominican businesses. The documents had previously been lodged with the National City Bank of New York in Ciudad Trujillo before the Superintendent requested their surrender.
subfiles.title: Translation of Dominican Diplomatic Note No. 14057
subfiles.to: Embassy of the United States of America, Ciudad Trujillo

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum referring the Dominican inquiry on the Yokohama Specie Bank liquidation to the State Department Legal Adviser.
subfiles.summary: P. R. Atterberry of the Foreign Funds Control Division forwards Ciudad Trujillo despatch no. 958 to Legal Adviser Green H. Hackworth, noting that the inquiry raises legal questions within the Legal Adviser's jurisdiction. The memorandum outlines that the Yokohama Specie Bank's New York branch is being liquidated by the New York Superintendent of Banks in conjunction with the Alien Property Custodian, and that the Treasury Department routinely refers such inquiries directly to the Superintendent. Atterberry requests that any reply prepared by the Legal Adviser be routed through FF for coordination.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Foreign Funds Control to Legal Adviser on Ciudad Trujillo Despatch

subfiles.about: Letter transmitting the Dominican inquiry to the New York Superintendent of Banks and requesting his comments on his legal capacity.
keywords: Superintendent of Banks of the State of New York
subfiles.summary: State Department Legal Adviser Green H. Hackworth forwards Ciudad Trujillo despatch no. 958 and the Dominican note to New York Superintendent of Banks William R. White. The letter highlights the Dominican Government's questions regarding White's legal capacity to receive commercial documents drawn by Sanko & Co., Ltd. of Osaka against firms in the Dominican Republic. Hackworth solicits White's official comments and position so that an appropriate diplomatic response may be provided.
subfiles.title: Letter from Legal Adviser Hackworth to New York Superintendent of Banks White

subfiles.about: Routing memorandum circulating the Dominican inquiry for departmental review and censorship clearance before dispatch.
subfiles.summary: F. Trail of the Division of Foreign Activity Correlation circulates the Ciudad Trujillo file among the Foreign Funds Control Division, DUA, the Division of American Republics Affairs, and the Division of Far Eastern Affairs. Departmental officers are requested to review the file and provide comments before returning it to FC. The memorandum notes that the communication must be submitted to the Office of Censorship prior to transmission to the New York State Banking Department.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip from Foreign Activity Correlation Circulating the Ciudad Trujillo File
subfiles.to: Foreign Funds Control Division, DUA, RA, Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Despatch from Buenos Aires transmitting information from the Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires regarding Japanese transactions.
keywords: Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires
subfiles.summary: A damaged and heavily corrupted despatch from the U.S. Embassy in Buenos Aires to the Secretary of State concerning financial operations of the Yokohama Specie Bank. The Embassy reports on communications with the Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires regarding Japanese bank drafts and transfers involving the Banco do Brasil. This despatch provides the core field report referenced in subsequent State Department correspondence on Yokohama Draft 1392.
subfiles.title: Despatch from American Embassy Buenos Aires on Yokohama Specie Bank Draft

subfiles.about: Photographic reproductions of financial drafts and banking documents related to the Yokohama Specie Bank.
keywords: Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires
subfiles.summary: This enclosure consists of photographic copies of five banking documents and financial records transmitted by the American Embassy at Buenos Aires. The exhibits document transactions between the Yokohama Specie Bank, the Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, and the Banco do Brasil. They corroborate the financial history and clearance of Yokohama Draft 1392.
subfiles.title: Photographic Exhibits of Banking Records from American Embassy Buenos Aires

subfiles.about: Cover sheet and mail registry records from the New York State Banking Department concerning the Yokohama Specie Bank.
keywords: Superintendent of Banks of the State of New York
subfiles.summary: This document bears the letterhead of New York Superintendent of Banks Elliott V. Bell alongside postal stamps, air mail registry entries, and indexing notations regarding the Yokohama Specie Bank. It reflects the administrative transmission of correspondence between state liquidation officials in New York and federal authorities. The markings illustrate the chain of custody for incoming and outgoing wartime financial records.
subfiles.title: Cover Sheet and Mail Registry on Yokohama Specie Bank Liquidation

subfiles.about: Letter transmitting confidential findings from Buenos Aires regarding payment of Yokohama Specie Bank Draft 1392.
keywords: Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires
subfiles.summary: Lloyd D. Yates, Acting Assistant Chief of the Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, writes to Mr. Murray of the New York State Banking Department in response to Murray's May 26, 1943 inquiry. Yates conveys confidential findings obtained via the American Embassy in Buenos Aires from the Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires. The Argentine institution reported that Yokohama Draft 1392 for $230.00 had been settled on July 7, 1941 via postal transfer into the account of the Banco do Brasil at the Guaranty Trust Company of New York.
subfiles.title: Letter from State Department to New York Banking Department on Yokohama Draft 1392

subfiles.about: Letter detailing the legal and supervisory basis for the New York Superintendent's liquidation of the Yokohama Specie Bank.
subfiles.summary: W. A. Lyon, Assistant to Superintendent Elliott V. Bell, replies to State Department Legal Adviser Green H. Hackworth's August 10 letter regarding the Dominican inquiry. Lyon explains that the Superintendent seized the New York Agency of the Yokohama Specie Bank in December 1941 pursuant to Section 606 of the New York Banking Law. He clarifies that the liquidation proceeded under a Treasury Department license issued January 14, 1942, which was superseded on September 28, 1942 by a supervisory order issued by the Alien Property Custodian.
subfiles.title: Letter from New York Banking Department Explaining Authority over Yokohama Specie Bank

subfiles.about: State Department instruction directing the mission at Ciudad Trujillo to inform the Dominican Government of the New York Superintendent's authority.
keywords: Superintendent of Banks of the State of New York
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State issues Instruction No. 627 to the American Mission at Ciudad Trujillo in reply to despatch no. 958. Enclosing the August 17, 1943 letter from the New York Banking Department, the instruction directs the mission to convey the substance of the Banking Department's explanation to the Dominican Foreign Office. This communication formally resolves the Dominican inquiry regarding the legal authority governing the liquidation of the Yokohama Specie Bank.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 627 to American Mission Ciudad Trujillo on Authority of Superintendent of Banks
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge of the American Mission, Ciudad Trujillo

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording an Alien Property Custodian letter on unblocking Yokohama Specie Bank assets in Honduras.
subfiles.summary: This State Department cross-reference file note indexes a letter dated December 18, 1944 from the Alien Property Custodian, filed under decimal number 840.51PC15/12-1844. The subject of the underlying document pertains to the unblocking of assets of the Yokohama Specie Bank in Honduras. It records the continuing administrative actions involving Japanese assets in Central America late in the war.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Unblocking Yokohama Specie Bank Assets in Honduras

subfiles.about: Memorandum on coordinating Japanese financial intelligence between the FBI, State Department, and Treasury.
subfiles.summary: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Adviser on Political Relations, inquires of Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle, Jr. whether the Department should verify if the FBI had provided certain intelligence information to the Treasury Department, or whether State should take steps to inform Treasury directly. Berle concurred with Hornbeck's suggestions, noting his handwritten affirmative reply: 'Yes - to both yous'. The exchange demonstrates early 1941 inter-agency monitoring of Japanese financial activities prior to open hostilities.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Hornbeck to Berle on Transmitting FBI Intelligence to the Treasury
